evals.prompt: I just cloned a Django repo I've never seen at ~/work/orderly and I have no idea where to start. Walk me through getting oriented.
evals.expected_output: A crawl that reads pyproject.toml or requirements.txt first, identifies manage.py and the WSGI or ASGI module as entry points, lists the top-level apps with a role each, and follows urls.py rather than listing directories.
assertions: The manifest file is read before any application source file
manage.py or the wsgi/asgi module is identified as an entry point
Top-level directories are listed with a one-line role for each
The response follows the URL configuration or imports rather than only listing folders
No build, install, or run command is executed against the repo

evals.prompt: how do i get up to speed on this monorepo fast
evals.expected_output: A crawl that maps package boundaries first from the workspace tooling, then treats each package as a smaller crawl, and sizes the job before planning depth.
assertions: The workspace or monorepo tooling file is identified to find package boundaries
Package boundaries are mapped before any single package is explored in depth
The response counts or estimates the size of the codebase before planning the crawl
The response states that repeated patterns will be sampled rather than read exhaustively

evals.prompt: Explore this repo. The README says it's a microservice architecture with a service layer, an API gateway, and event-driven communication.
evals.expected_output: A crawl that treats the README as a claim to verify, checking the import graph and the code for real service boundaries and event usage rather than repeating the README.
assertions: The response states that the README claims will be verified against the code
The verification follows imports or looks for actual queue, event, or HTTP client usage
Any gap between the README description and the code is recorded as a finding
Directory names alone are not treated as proof of the described architecture
